worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $a,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut+\frac{1}{2}a{t}^{2},
$$

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle and $u$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=0i+0j,\,u=2i+6j,\,a=i+5j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the rocket after $t=2\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(0i+0j)+(2i+6j)(2)+\frac{1}{2}(i+5j)(2)^{2} \\  & =(4i+12j)+2(i+5j) \\  & =(4i+12j)+(2i+10j) \\  & =(\,6\,i+22\,j)\,\text{m}.\end{aligned}
$$
